summary: Blind second coding of 109 review studies from abstracts plus full-text check of 52 open-access papers

fulltext.notes: Full text not accessible: ScienceDirect PDF and article pages returned HTTP 403; DOI resolved via linkinghub to a redirect stub only. No full-text coding possible.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: Discussion end: "This research has a few limitations. First, it uses a cross-sectional survey to approve the proposed research model."
fulltext.sample: 191 valid responses (312 sent, 220 returned) from middle/senior managers of Jordanian manufacturing firms, Q1 2025; Jordan; PLS-SEM
fulltext.notes: Full text agrees with the abstract. The full title adds that industry dynamism moderates the link (H3 supported, β=0.19). The direct AIC to CA path is β=0.38, p<0.001. Agility partially mediates (β=0.21). CA is not framed as sustainable as the dependent variable.
The DOI redirects to the linkinghub.elsevier.com page, which only showed "Redirecting". The ScienceDirect article page and the PDF both returned HTTP 403, so the full text could not be read.
Full text not reached: DOI redirects through linkinghub (redirect placeholder only) to ScienceDirect, which returned HTTP 403. No other candidate URL was available.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: Section 6 "Limitations and Avenues for Future Research": "this study relies on cross-sectional survey data"
fulltext.sample: 432 usable online-survey responses from MSME owners, managers and supervisors (the abstract says 350); country not stated, but the authors are at Universitas Putera Batam, Indonesia
fulltext.notes: The abstract gives n=350, but the methods report 432. Table 4 gives AI to CA as beta=0.284, p=0.000. Figure 2 instead shows 0.130 on a dashed path, and its labels do not match the hypothesised model. The country is never named.
Full text not accessible: MDPI PDF, DOI redirect (mdpi.com landing page) and /htm all returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. Title suggests resilience (RES) outcome, but this was not verified from the text.
DOI redirected to journals.sagepub.com; landing, /doi/full and /doi/pdf all returned HTTP 403. Full text not accessible.

Full text not accessed: DOI redirected to linkinghub (only "Redirecting" stub), ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403. A curl retry was blocked as bot-check circumvention, so nothing was coded from the full text.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: Section "Limitations and future research": "This study has several limitations that warrant further investigation."
fulltext.sample: 229 Chinese high-tech firms (Zhongguancun, Harbin, Chengdu, Shenzhen); senior and R&D managers; three-wave survey; China
fulltext.notes: AIC is tested only as a moderator. Its main effect on SCP is non-significant (Table 5, Model 6: b=0.05, ns), and H4 (DI x AIC to SCP) is not supported. AIC raises DI and moderates SEO to DI positively.
All SAGE URLs returned HTTP 403 (PDF download, DOI landing, and /doi/full/); the DOI redirect led to the same blocked domain. Full text not accessed.
DOI redirects to Wiley Online Library; landing, /doi/full, /doi/pdf and /doi/epdf all returned HTTP 403, so the main text could not be read.

DOI goes to the USF Digital Commons landing page, which shows only the abstract. The PDF returned HTTP 403 (bot check), so the full text was not read. The abstract mentions 120 Tunisian family firms and says AI capabilities significantly enhance performance.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: Conclusion: "This research has several limitations, including its conceptual nature. The four-stage model we present is theoretical and not empirically tested."
fulltext.sample: - (conceptual paper, no empirical sample; US small business context, illustrative cases only)
fulltext.notes: The full text agrees with the abstract. It is a conceptual RBV/stakeholder-theory paper. Its four-stage roadmap ends with a transformation stage that develops dynamic capabilities and yields sustained competitive advantage. That makes the AI-to-SCA link partly conditional rather than purely negative.
MDPI PDF, DOI redirect (mdpi.com/2071-1050/18/3/1157) and /htm all returned HTTP 403; full text not accessible.
Handle redirects to cris.unibo.it, which returned HTTP 403 Forbidden; full text not accessible.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: The abstract says limitations are discussed, but there is no limitations section. The Conclusion only says "Future empirical studies are needed to verify the proposed relationships".
fulltext.notes: This is a proposed framework with no real data. The Results section (n=246, PLS-SEM) is explicitly "simulated", with values the authors call "fake". The mixed-methods survey is only planned, and AI is proposed to raise performance through innovation capability.
MDPI PDF and article page both returned HTTP 403; DOI redirected to the blocked MDPI page. Full text not accessed.
The handle URL returned HTTP 404 over both http and https. No full text was accessed.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: Section 3.8 "Methodological Limitations": "survey relies on self-reported data, which may introduce response bias"
fulltext.sample: 312 senior managers/strategy professionals (survey) plus 28 interviews in 12 medium and large firms; Zimbabwe
fulltext.notes: The paper reports partial mediation by CI and says AI acts "both directly and indirectly", but it never reports the direct AI-to-outcome coefficient. The discussion also says AI alone may not directly improve performance. The two DVs are corporate growth and sustainability performance.
MDPI PDF and article page both returned HTTP 403; DOI redirected to the blocked MDPI page. Full text not accessed.
Both candidate URLs (PDF and DOI redirect to tandfonline full text) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden; full text not accessible.
The DOI redirected to onlinelibrary.wiley.com, which returned HTTP 403 for both the landing page and the /doi/full/ page. The full text could not be read.

fulltext.sample: 280 valid responses (of 500 distributed) from employees of financial institutions, Saudi Arabia
fulltext.notes: The abstract reports 180 employees but the methods report 280 valid responses. H1 (AI capability to organizational performance) is supported: beta 0.35, t 4.38, p<0.001.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: "Several limitations should be acknowledged." (end of discussion/conclusion section)
fulltext.sample: 385 banking professionals from ~71 commercial banks; Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Philippines, Vietnam (ASEAN-5); cross-sectional survey, PLS-SEM
fulltext.notes: AI-enabled risk analytics has a significant direct effect on bank financial performance (p<0.01, small f2). FinTech adoption partially mediates the effect. Performance is measured subjectively (profitability, efficiency, market share).
MDPI PDF and HTML full text both returned HTTP 403; DOI redirected to the same blocked MDPI page. Full text not accessed.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: 6.3 Limitations and Future Scope of Research: "yet it suffers from limitations."
fulltext.sample: 326 managers from 17 BSE-listed organizations, India (survey, PLS-SEM)
fulltext.notes: The outcomes are AI-CRM implementation, acceptance and failure, not firm performance or competitive advantage. Technology turbulence moderates the paths. No hypothesis is reported as rejected. Coefficients for H5 and H7 could not be checked because Table 4 was missing from the page text.
Both URLs redirect to link.springer.com, which then redirects to a cookie-based idp.springer.com authorization step; full text could not be retrieved.
DOI redirects to SSRN; abstract page and PDF delivery both returned HTTP 403, so full text not accessible.
Wiley PDF and landing page both returned HTTP 403; DOI redirected to the blocked Wiley page. Full text not accessed.
Wiley pdfdirect and landing page both returned HTTP 403; DOI redirected to the blocked Wiley page. Full text not accessed.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: Section "Limitations and Future Research": "solely pays attention to e-commerce firms in China"; cross-sectional data.
fulltext.sample: 394 valid questionnaires (441 received) from e-commerce/online retail firms (entrepreneurs, executives), China
fulltext.notes: No direct AIC-to-FP path was estimated. AIC-to-AIDDM (H4) was non-significant, and so was the simple mediation AIC-AIDDM-FP (0.015, t=0.591). The effect is positive only through the FC/AIM-AIDDM chains. The authors state that AIC "does not directly affect firm performance".
DOI redirected to Elsevier linkinghub (returned only a "Redirecting" stub); ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403. Full text not accessible.

fulltext.sample: 15 registered clothing MSME owners (semi-structured interviews), Bulacan, Philippines
fulltext.notes: Qualitative hermeneutic-phenomenological study framed by DCT (sensing/seizing/transforming). There is no study-limitations section: the "limitations" it mentions are limits of the free AI tools. The conclusion claims a "sustainable competitive advantage", but no significance tests were run.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: Conclusions: "The study also has limitations. It is based on three case studies and secondary data"
fulltext.sample: 3 firms (Siemens AG, Schneider Electric SE, Krka d.d.); qualitative multiple-case study of secondary documents; Germany, France, Slovenia (Europe)
fulltext.notes: Full title says "European Industrial Firms". Discussion stresses AI "does not automatically confer a competitive advantage"; value depends on digital maturity and governance. Krka builds competitiveness mainly without AI. Qualitative, so no significance testing.

Conceptual paper (Teece and Pitelis, MIR 2026). The only "limitations" discussed are those of internalization theory, not of the paper itself; Section 6 lists future research directions. AI ecosystem participation creates new forms of competitive advantage, with orchestration as the mechanism.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: Section 6.4 "Limitations and future research": "Our findings are based on data from SMEs in China."
fulltext.notes: The outcome is international competitive advantage (product innovation advantage and brand upgrading advantage), plus GVC upgrading in robustness checks. The AI adoption–strategic agility coupling directly affects PIA and BUA (H1a/H1b supported). H5a and H6b (moderation) are not supported. Nothing contradicts the abstract.
DOI redirected to journals.sagepub.com, which returned HTTP 403 for both the landing and PDF pages; full text not accessible.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: Conclusions, final paragraph: "this article highlights those AI implementations that prove successful... businesses rarely disclose failed implementations"
fulltext.sample: - (descriptive multi-method: literature review, secondary data and illustrative company examples such as Allegro, Amazon, Netflix, Spotify and Shopify; Polish market)
fulltext.notes: The "case studies" are only a short descriptive table of five firms built from secondary sources, and none are Polish SMEs. There is no empirical testing. The limitation is noted briefly in one paragraph of the conclusions, not in its own section. The conclusions also say AI helps build sustainable competitive advantage.

fulltext.sample: 28 in-depth interviews with T&A/RMG managers, IT consultants, academics and industry experts, Bangladesh (plus systematic literature review)
fulltext.notes: No limitations section; the conclusion has only one future-research sentence about quantitative testing. "Limitations" in the text refers to limits of AI, not of the study. Qualitative design: AI becomes a dynamic capability (agility) for competitive advantage once tangible and intangible resources are integrated.
